requirements.text: The vehicle bumper shall be struck at 40 km/h with a legform that simulates the impact response of an adult's leg.
Vehicles with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm shall be tested with a lower legform.
Vehicles with a lower bumper height of more than 500 mm shall be tested with an upper legform test device.
Vehicles with a lower bumper height between 425 mm and 500 mm shall be tested with either the lower legform or the upper legform, chosen by the manufacturer.
In the lower legform to bumper test, the vehicle shall meet limits on lateral knee bending angle, knee shearing displacement and lateral tibia acceleration.
In the upper legform to bumper test, the vehicle shall meet limits on the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time and on the bending moment.

The vehicle bumper shall meet minimum performance requirements for leg protection by subjecting pedestrians to lower impact forces when impacted by a legform impactor that simulates the leg of a mid-size adult male.
The vehicle bumper shall be evaluated by impact with either a lower legform impactor or an upper legform impactor, depending on the height of the bumper.
The impact speed for both the lower legform and upper legform tests to the bumper shall be 40 km/h.
Vehicles with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm to a reference line on the lower surface of the bumper shall be tested with the lower legform impactor.
Upper legform to bumper tests shall be carried out if the lower bumper height is more than 500 mm.
For vehicles that have a lower bumper height between 425 mm and 500 mm, either a lower legform test or an upper legform test, as elected by the vehicle manufacturer, shall be performed.
In the lower legform to bumper test, the maximum lateral knee bending angle shall be ≤ 19.0°.
In the lower legform to bumper test, the maximum lateral knee shearing displacement shall be ≤ 6.0 mm.
In the lower legform to bumper test, the maximum lateral tibia acceleration shall be ≤ 170g.
The bumper shall meet the maximum lateral tibia acceleration limit of 170g except within bumper test widths nominated by the manufacturer of up to 264 mm in total.
Within the manufacturer-nominated bumper test widths of up to 264 mm in total, the acceleration measured at the upper end of the tibia shall not exceed 250g.
Vehicles with a lower bumper height of more than 500 mm shall be subject to an upper legform test requiring the bumper to be energy absorbing.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm, the lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.1. shall be applied.

For vehicles with a lower bumper height greater than, or equal to, 425 mm and less than 500 mm, either the lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.1. or the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer, shall be applied.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height of greater than, or equal to, 500 mm, the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.2. shall be applied.

Compliance of the bumper with the lower legform to bumper performance requirements specified in paragraph 5.1.1. shall be verified using the test impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1. and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.1.

For vehicles with a lower bumper height greater than or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm where the upper legform to bumper test is applied, compliance with the performance requirements specified in paragraph 5.1.2. shall be verified using the test impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.2. and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.2.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.

Where the manufacturer nominates bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total, the absolute value of the tibia bending moment within those widths shall not exceed 380 Nm when tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper).
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2. (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2. (upper legform to bumper), the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.
When the vehicle is tested as a DPPS (deployable pedestrian protection system) in headform tests, the test conditions and requirements in Annex 1 shall apply.

Where a cut-body is used for the test, the cut-body shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure, all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user, to demonstrate the performance and interactions of all the contributory vehicle components.
Where a cut-body is used for the test, the cut-body shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.
All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
The manufacturer shall show that any devices designed to protect vulnerable road users will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

For vehicle components which could change shape or position, other than active devices to protect pedestrians, and which have more than one fixed shape or position, the vehicle shall comply with the components in each fixed shape or position.
When tested as a DPPS, the vehicle shall be adjusted as specified in the test procedure defined in Annex 1.
For the flexible lower legform impactor to bumper test, the selected target points shall be in the bumper test area.

For the flexible lower legform impactor to bumper test, the direction of the impact velocity vector shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ± 2° in the horizontal plane and in the longitudinal plane at the time of first contact.

For the flexible lower legform impactor to bumper test, the axis of the impactor shall be perpendicular to the horizontal plane, with a roll and pitch angle tolerance of ± 2° in the lateral and longitudinal plane.

For the flexible lower legform impactor to bumper test, the bottom of the impactor (without parts needed for the purposes of launching and/or protection) shall be 75 mm ± 10 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of the first contact with the bumper.
The bumper shall meet the flexible lower legform impactor to bumper test requirements at an impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper of 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
The impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
If all of the prerequisites are met, the vehicle fitted with a DPPS shall be tested with the DPPS activated as intended for the entire headform test area.
If any of the prerequisites from paragraphs 1.2 to 1.7 of Annex 1 are not met, the vehicle fitted with a DPPS shall be tested with the DPPS in the undeployed position.

For protection below the lower deployment threshold speed of the DPPS, the vehicle shall meet the headform test procedures specified in paragraphs 7.2 to 7.4 with the impact speed specified at 0.9 times the lower deployment threshold speed, where the allocation of the HIC1700 and HIC1000 Zones may differ from those at nominal velocity (9.7 m/s) headform impact tests according to paragraph 5.2.4.
In the headform test for protection below the lower deployment threshold speed of the DPPS, the HIC shall comply with paragraph 5.2.3. of the Regulation.
The lowest speed of activation (lower deployment velocity threshold) of the DPPS shall be specified by the vehicle manufacturer.

For the system deployment verification of the DPPS, sensor activation tests with the FlexPLI, as specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1. of this Regulation, shall be performed within the detection test area at the DPPS lower deployment velocity threshold.
For DPPS sensing system verification, a test with the FlexPLI shall be performed at nominal velocity (11.1m/s) at vehicle centreline (Y0).
If the DPPS is not activated during any of the sensing system verification tests, all headform tests shall be conducted in undeployed position according to paragraphs 7.2. to 7.4. of this Regulation.
The total response time (TRT) of the DPPS shall be confirmed by using the FlexPLI at the vehicle speed of 11.1 m/s and at the vehicle centreline (Y0).
If the measured sensing time (ST) of the DPPS is within a tolerance of -5ms/+3ms of the value specified by the manufacturer, the value specified by the manufacturer shall be used.
If the measured sensing time (ST) of the DPPS is not within a tolerance of -5ms/+3ms of the value specified by the manufacturer, the measured value shall be used for the test.
For dynamic testing of the DPPS, only the sensing time (ST) shall be verified.

Where the combined static and dynamic test option is chosen by the manufacturer and the headform test area consists of sections where the HIT_d at the corresponding impact point is less than TRT (HIT_d < TRT) and sections where the HIT_d is greater than or equal to TRT (HIT_d ≥ TRT), all test points of the DPPS forward of the corresponding WAD (HIT_d < TRT) shall be tested dynamically.
The ESA sample(s) submitted for ESA type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.

In case an ESA is (part of) a light source, the ESA shall either have an approval number granted according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128, or be shown by a test report from a Technical Service designated by the Type Approval Authority to be not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
ESAs which are intentional RF transmitters and which have not received type approval in conjunction with a vehicle manufacturer shall be supplied with suitable installation guidelines.

An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under UN Regulation No. 10, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN Regulation No. 10.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the ESA broadband type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the ESA narrowband type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

For the stripline method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.

For the TEM cell method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency range.

For the BCI method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.

For the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range.

For the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 10 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.

For the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 21 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range.

For the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall be immune at a test level of 7 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, and at a minimum test level of 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.

The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9 in order to be considered as complying with immunity requirements.

The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

The ESA shall meet the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1 for the starting profile and the Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the starting profile test, which is only applicable to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall meet immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, with functional status B for immunity related functions of ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases, functional status C for immunity related functions of other ESA, and functional status D for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 1, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -75 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems with 500 pulses, with FPSC III for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +37 V for 12 V systems and +37 V for 24 V systems with 500 pulses, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +10 V for 12 V systems and +20 V for 24 V systems with 10 pulses, with FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -112 V for 12 V systems and -150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9.

ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
RF transmitters shall be tested in the transmit mode.

Spurious emissions of RF transmitters shall be subject to the requirements of this Regulation, whereas wanted emissions (e.g. from RF transmitting systems) within the necessary bandwidth and out of band emissions are disregarded.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be so designed, constructed and fitted as to enable the vehicle, in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

The vehicle shall comply with the radiated emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).

The vehicle shall comply with the radiated emission limits given in paragraphs 6.2. and 7.2. of the Regulation for quasi-peak detectors, with a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 applied if peak detectors are used.
The vehicle shall meet the narrowband electromagnetic emission requirements when tested according to CISPR 12, if not otherwise stated in Annex 5.
During the narrowband emission test, the vehicle ignition switch shall be switched on.
During the narrowband emission test, the vehicle engine shall not be operating.
During the narrowband emission test, the vehicle's electronic systems shall all be in normal operating mode with the vehicle stationary.

During the narrowband emission test, all equipment which can be switched on permanently by the driver or passenger with internal oscillators > 9 kHz or repetitive signals should be in normal operation.

The vehicle narrowband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).

The vehicle electronic systems shall demonstrate immunity when the vehicle is subjected to electromagnetic fields according to ISO 11451-2 in an ALSE with front irradiation, for vehicles not considered as "large vehicles", at the test levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of the Regulation.

In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with vehicle speed 50 km/h (respectively 25 km/h for L1, L2 vehicles) ±20 per cent, the vehicle shall not exhibit a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed, and in case of automatic gearbox shall not exhibit a change of gear ratio inducing a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with dipped beams ON (manual mode), the vehicle shall not exhibit lighting OFF (front light and rear light).
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with specific warning (e.g. rotating/flashing light, signalling bar, siren) OFF, the vehicle shall not exhibit specific warning ON.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the cluster operating in normal mode, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected warning or an inconsistent variation of the odometer.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, the rear view system shall not exhibit unexpected movement of the rear view mirror or loss or freezing of the display (CMS).
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the front wiper ON (manual mode) at maximum speed, the vehicle shall not exhibit a complete stop of the front wiper.

In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the direction indicator on the driver's side ON, the direction indicator shall not exhibit a frequency change (lower than 0.75 Hz or greater than 2.25 Hz) or a duty cycle change (lower than 25 per cent or greater than 75 per cent).
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with adjustable suspension in normal position, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected significant variation.

In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the driver's seat and steering wheel in medium position, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected variation greater than 10 per cent of total range.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the alarm unset, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected activation of the alarm.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the horn OFF, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected activation of the horn.

In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with airbag and safety restraint systems operational with inhibited passenger airbag if this function exists, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected activation.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with automatic doors closed, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected opening.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the adjustable endurance brake lever in normal position, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected activation.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with the brake pedal not depressed, the vehicle shall not exhibit an unexpected activation of brake or an unexpected activation of stop lights.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, with ADS operational, the ADS shall not remain in a failure safe mode or expected failure operational mode.
The ESA under test for broadband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The broadband radiated emission limits for the ESA shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
The ESA under test for narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The ESA radiated narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall comply with the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

ESAs shall comply with the immunity requirements of any combination, at the manufacturer's discretion, of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 or reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.

ESAs in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall comply with the requirements of the combination of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2 and bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.
The ESA shall be tested under test conditions according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity tests.
The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
The ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.

The ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.

The ESA shall be immune to the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, except for ESAs that are exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor).

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on the supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position of less than 425 mm, the bumper shall meet the flexible lower legform to bumper requirements.

For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position greater than, or equal to, 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the bumper shall meet either the flexible lower legform to bumper requirements or the upper legform to bumper requirements, at the choice of the manufacturer.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position greater than, or equal to, 500 mm, the bumper shall meet the upper legform to bumper requirements.

When the bumper is tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1, the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.

When the bumper is tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1, the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
When the bumper is tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1, the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.
Where the manufacturer nominates bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total as a relaxation zone, the absolute value of the tibia bending moment in those widths shall not exceed 380 Nm.
When the bumper is tested with the upper legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2, the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When the bumper is tested with the upper legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2, the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.

When tested with the child and adult headforms in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the combined bonnet top test area and the windscreen test area, measuring points in the cowl monitoring area not being taken into consideration.
When tested with the child and adult headforms in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two-thirds of the bonnet top test area.
When tested with the child and adult headforms in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, the HIC for the remaining test areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both headforms.
In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area.
In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC for the remaining area shall not exceed 1,700.
When tested with the child headform in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3 and 4, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area.
When tested with the child headform in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3 and 4, the HIC for the remaining areas shall not exceed 1,700.

In the case of a vehicle fitted with an ARHSS which could change the vehicle height at the front axle more than 20 mm from the nominal for any vehicle speed between 25 and 40 km/h, compliance with the biomechanical limits of the flexible lower legform to bumper and upper legform to bumper requirements respectively shall be demonstrated, with the agreement of the technical service, by a limited number of legform tests or by numerical simulation.

In the case of a vehicle fitted with an ARHSS which could change the vehicle height at the front axle more than 20 mm from the nominal for any vehicle speed between 25 and 40 km/h, compliance with the HIC 1,700 requirement on the additional head test area shall be demonstrated, with the agreement of the technical service, by a limited number of head impact tests or by numerical simulation.

The vehicle used for the pedestrian protection test shall be in its normal ride attitude, and shall be either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.

Where a cut-body is used for the pedestrian protection test, the cut-body shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure, all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user, to demonstrate the performance and interactions of all the contributory vehicle components.
Where a cut-body is used for the pedestrian protection test, the cut-body shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.
All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
The manufacturer shall show that any devices designed to protect vulnerable road users will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

For vehicle components which could change shape or position, other than active devices to protect pedestrians, and which have more than one fixed shape or position, the vehicle shall comply with the pedestrian protection requirements with the components in each fixed shape or position.

The bumper shall meet the lower legform to bumper test requirements with the impact velocity vector in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±2° in the horizontal and longitudinal plane at the time of first contact, and with the impactor axis perpendicular to the horizontal plane within a roll and pitch angle tolerance of ±2° in the lateral and longitudinal plane.

The bumper shall meet the lower legform to bumper test requirements with the bottom of the impactor (without parts needed for the purposes of launching and/or protection) at 75 mm ± 10 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of first contact with the bumper.
The bumper shall meet the lower legform to bumper test requirements when struck by the impactor at an impact velocity of 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
The impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the lighting and signalling devices of the vehicle shall continue to operate correctly and to remain visible, where disturbed adjustment of factory-fitted lighting devices may be corrected to conform to the required specifications provided this can be done by the normal means of adjustment, and bulbs may be replaced in the event of filament failure.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the vehicle's bonnet (hood), boot lid (trunk lid) and doors shall be operable in the normal manner.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the side doors of the vehicle shall not be able to open under the effect of the impact.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the vehicle's fuel and cooling systems shall have neither leaks nor constricted fluid passages which prevent normal functioning.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the sealing devices and caps of the vehicle's fuel and cooling systems shall be operable in the normal manner.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the vehicle's exhaust system shall not suffer any damage or displacement which would prevent its normal function.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3, the vehicle's propulsion, suspension (including tyres), steering and braking systems shall remain in adjustment and shall operate in a normal manner, except that sensors, cameras, radar devices, etc. being part of driver assist systems may become damaged, disoriented or broken due to an impact carried out according to Annex 3 as long as the basic braking and steering performance are still intact.
For the impact test according to Annex 3, the front wheels of the vehicle shall be in the straight-ahead position.
For the impact test according to Annex 3, the tyres of the vehicle shall be inflated to the pressure recommended by the vehicle manufacturer.
For the impact test according to Annex 3, the brakes of the vehicle shall be disengaged and the transmission control shall be in neutral position.

Vehicles equipped with hydro pneumatic, hydraulic or pneumatic suspension or a device for automatic levelling according to load shall be tested in the impact test according to Annex 3 in the normal running conditions specified by the manufacturer.
The first contact of the impactor with the vehicle shall be by the impact contour on the protective device.

In the two vehicle-loading conditions, the protective device between the corners, as defined in paragraph 3.1.5. of UN R42, shall be intersected by the horizontal plane passing through the reference line of the impactor.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.
The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that it is not possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

In the case of side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.

In the case of all signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall comply when verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and, in the case where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except for a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the requirements for lamps constituting a pair shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

Where lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, shall be fulfilled.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, except for a single retro-reflector.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of two lamps or two independent retro reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system, except that a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.
Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall extend on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
The illumination of the surface of two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.

Where the light-emitting surface of two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip is constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements, these individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
The maximum height above the ground of a lamp shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
Direction-indicator lamps shall be flashing lamps.
The vehicle-hazard warning signal shall be a flashing lamp.
Amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7. shall be flashing lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be a flashing lamp.

Where the photometric characteristics of any lamp vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

Where the photometric characteristics of a direction indicator lamp of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a or 2b are varied during a flash by sequential activation of light sources, this shall be as specified in paragraph 5.6. of UN Regulation No. 6 or paragraph 5.6.11. of UN Regulation No. [LSD].

The variation of photometric characteristics during a flash by sequential activation of light sources shall not be applied when direction indicator lamps of categories 2a and 2b are operated as emergency stop signal according to paragraph 6.23.1.

The lamp(s) used for answer-back signal, which may flash and/or vary in luminous intensity and/or vary in apparent surface, shall operate according to the conditions specified in general specifications and/or in dedicated paragraph 6.27.
White light emitted by a lamp fitted on the front of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the rear of the vehicle.

With the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirement on visibility of red light to the front and white light to the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.
The colour of the light emitted by the direction-indicator lamp shall be amber.
The colour of the light emitted by the hazard warning signal shall be amber.
The colour of the light emitted by the front position lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the parking lamp shall be white in front, red at the rear, and amber if reciprocally incorporated in the side direction-indicator lamps or in the side-marker lamps.

The colour of the light emitted by the side-marker lamp shall be amber; however the rearmost side-marker lamp can be red if it is grouped or combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop lamp or is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retro-reflector.
The colour of the light emitted by the end-outline marker lamp shall be white in front and red at the rear.
The colour of the light emitted by the daytime running lamp shall be white.
The colour of the front retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be identical to incident light (also known as white or colourless retro-reflector).

The colour of the side retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be amber; however the rearmost side retro-reflector can be red if it is grouped or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear position lamp, the rear end outline marker lamp, the rear fog lamp, the stop-lamp, the red rearmost side-marker lamp or the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular.

The colour of the light emitted by the exterior courtesy lamp shall be white and, in addition, in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the exterior courtesy lamp.
The colour of the light emitted by the manoeuvring lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.

Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

The vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement of light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 37 in lamps fitted to the vehicle.

Where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

For vehicles of M and N categories, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of devices indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

For vehicles of M and N categories, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant, in all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by the special power supply/electronic light source control gear, secondary operating mode or applicant-requested voltage provision, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent, where the means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the device may be located within the body of the device.

The terminal voltage limits for devices indicated in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7. shall not apply to devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, except for obstacles already presented when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device, and proof thereof shall be furnished.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

All lamps (devices) installed on a vehicle shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN R48.
In case of light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps installed on a vehicle approved according to UN R48 and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only, except that this does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources unless they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.
Lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) shall be used exclusively in the case where the statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8. is present and positive.
Lamps related to the use of LED substitute light source(s) shall bear the marking related to the use of LED substitute light source(s).
The direction-indicator lamps shall be mandatory on the vehicle.
Arrangement "A" of direction-indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 5 and 6) shall apply to all motor vehicles.
The number of direction-indicator lamps shall be according to the arrangement.

The direction-indicator lamps shall be type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 6, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For arrangement A, the two front direction-indicator lamps shall be of category 1 or 1a or 1b if the distance between the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of this lamp and that of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or the front fog lamp, if there is one, is at least 40 mm.

For arrangement A, the two front direction-indicator lamps shall be of category 1a or 1b if the distance between the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of this lamp and that of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or the front fog lamp, if there is one, is greater than 20 mm and less than 40 mm.

For arrangement A, the two front direction-indicator lamps shall be of category 1b if the distance between the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of this lamp and that of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or the front fog lamp, if there is one, is less than or equal to 20 mm.
For arrangement A, two rear direction-indicator lamps of category 2a or 2b shall be fitted.
For arrangement A, two side direction-indicator lamps of category 5 (minimum requirement) shall be fitted for all M1 vehicles and for N1, M2 and M3 vehicles not exceeding 6 metres in length.
Category 5 side direction-indicator lamps may be replaced by category 6 side direction-indicator lamps in all instances.

Where lamps combining the functions of front direction-indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b) and side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) are fitted, two additional side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) may be fitted to meet the visibility requirements of paragraph 6.5.5.

Where an AFS is fitted, the distance to be considered for the choice of the front direction-indicator lamp category shall be the distance between the front direction-indicator lamp and the closest lighting unit in its closest position contributing to or performing a passing-beam mode.

The edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the direction-indicator lamp farthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except for the optional rear lamps.

The distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes of the direction-indicator lamps shall not be less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

The height above the ground of the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6 shall not be less than 350 mm for M1 and N1 category of vehicles and 500 mm for all other categories of vehicles, measured from the lowest point.
The height above the ground of the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 or 6 shall not be more than 1,500 mm, measured from the highest point.
The height above the ground of the direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b, measured in accordance with paragraph 5.8., shall not be less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm.

If the structure of the vehicle does not permit the upper height limit to be respected and if the optional rear lamps are not installed, the upper height limit for side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 and 6 may be increased to 2,300 mm.

If the structure of the vehicle does not permit the upper height limit to be respected and if the optional rear lamps are not installed, the upper height limit for direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b may be increased to 2,100 mm.

The distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp (categories 5 and 6) and the transverse plane which marks the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 1,800 mm.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, the distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp (categories 5 and 6) and the transverse plane which marks the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 2,500 mm.

For all other categories of vehicles, if the structure of the vehicle makes it impossible to comply with the minimum angles of visibility, the distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp (categories 5 and 6) and the transverse plane which marks the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 2,500 mm.
Optional category 5 side direction indicator lamps shall be fitted, spaced evenly, along the length of the vehicle.

The vertical angles of geometric visibility of direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b and 5 shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1) the downward angle may be reduced to 5° and where an optional rear lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1) the upward angle may be reduced to 5°.
The vertical angles of geometric visibility of direction indicator lamps of category 6 shall be 30° above and 5° below the horizontal.

The horizontal angles of geometric visibility of direction indicator lamps shall be as shown in the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.1, with the dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator not exceeding 5° up to d ≤ 1.80 m (for M1 and N1 category vehicles d ≤ 2.50 m), and for direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Where, at the discretion of the manufacturer, the alternative arrangement for M1 and N1 category vehicles is used, the horizontal angles of geometric visibility of front and rear direction indicator lamps, as well as side-marker lamps, shall be as shown in the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.2, with the dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator not exceeding 5° up to d ≤ 2.50 m, and for direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Where the alternative arrangement for M1 and N1 category vehicles is used, the vertical angles of geometric visibility of front and rear direction indicator lamps and side-marker lamps shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1) the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.

To be considered visible, the direction indicator lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, except for side direction-indicators of categories 5 and 6, with the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light excluded.
Direction-indicator lamps shall switch ON independently of the other lamps.
All direction-indicator lamps on one side of a vehicle shall be switched ON and OFF automatically as defined by applicable UN Regulations and/or by means of one control.
All direction-indicator lamps on one side of a vehicle shall flash in phase.

On M1 and N1 vehicles less than 6 m in length, with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2, the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall also flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the direction-indicator lamps.
A direction indicator capable of being activated in different modes (static or sequential) shall not switch between both modes once activated.
An operating tell-tale, visual or auditory or both, shall be provided for direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b.

If the direction-indicator operating tell-tale is visual, it shall be a flashing light which, at least in the event of the malfunction of any of these direction-indicator lamps, is either extinguished, or remains alight without flashing, or shows a marked change of frequency.

If the direction-indicator operating tell-tale is entirely auditory, it shall be clearly audible and shall show a marked change of frequency, at least in the event of the malfunction of any of these direction-indicator lamps.

The direction-indicator operating tell-tale shall be activated by the signal produced according to paragraph 6.2.2. of UN Regulation No. 6, or paragraph 5.6.3. of the 00 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148, or paragraph 4.6.1.4. of the 01 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148, or another suitable way.

If a motor vehicle is equipped to draw a trailer, it shall be fitted with a special visual operational tell-tale for the direction-indicator lamps on the trailer unless the tell-tale of the drawing vehicle allows the failure of any one of the direction-indicator lamps on the vehicle combination thus formed to be detected.
The direction-indicator light shall be a flashing light flashing 90 ± 30 times per minute.

Operation of the direction-indicator light-signal control shall be followed within not more than one second by the emission of light and within not more than one and one-half seconds by its first extinction.
If a motor vehicle is equipped to draw a trailer, the control of the direction-indicator lamps on the drawing vehicle shall also operate the indicator lamps of the trailer.

In the event of failure, other than short-circuit, of one direction-indicator lamp, the other direction-indicator lamps shall continue to flash, but the frequency in this condition may be different from that prescribed.
The hazard warning signal shall be fitted (mandatory).
The hazard warning signal shall be given by simultaneous operation of the direction-indicator lamps in accordance with the requirements of paragraph 6.5.
All direction indicators of category 1 (1, 1a, 1b) activated simultaneously as hazard warning signal shall operate in the same mode, i.e. static or sequential.
All direction indicators of category 2 (2a, 2b) activated simultaneously as hazard warning signal shall operate in the same mode, i.e. static or sequential.
The position in width of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.1.
The height of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.2.
The length position of the hazard warning signal lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4.3.
The hazard warning signal shall be operated by means of a separate manual control enabling all the direction-indicator lamps to flash in phase.

Where the hazard warning signal is switched ON automatically to indicate to other road-users the risk of imminent danger as defined by Regulations, the signal shall remain switched ON until it is manually or automatically switched OFF.

On M1 and N1 vehicles less than 6 m in length, with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2., the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall also flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the direction-indicator lamps when the hazard warning signal is operated.
The hazard warning signal shall meet the other requirements as specified in paragraph 6.5.9.
If a power-driven vehicle is equipped to draw a trailer, the hazard warning signal control shall also be capable of bringing the direction-indicator lamps on the trailer into action.
The hazard warning signal shall be able to function even if the device which starts or stops the propulsion system is in a position which makes it impossible to start the propulsion system.
The front position lamp shall be mandatory on all motor vehicles.

For the front position lamp, that point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

The front position lamp shall be positioned in height above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm for O1 and O2 categories of vehicles, or if for any other categories of vehicles the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).

Where the front position lamp and another lamp are reciprocally incorporated, the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the other lamp shall be used to verify compliance of the front position lamp with the positioning requirements of paragraphs 6.9.4.1. to 6.9.4.3.

The front position lamp shall have a geometric visibility horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane, and in the case of trailers the angle inwards may be reduced to 5°.

The front position lamp shall have a geometric visibility vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative at the discretion of the manufacturer and only if a front side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the front position lamp shall have a geometric visibility horizontal angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles using this alternative, only if a front side-marker lamp is installed, the front position lamp shall have a geometric visibility vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles using this alternative, to be considered visible the front position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm2, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.

A non-flashing closed-circuit tell-tale shall be provided for the front position lamps, except where the instrument panel lighting can only switch ON simultaneously with the front position lamps, and except while the daytime running lamps are switched ON.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the front position lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
Side-marker lamps shall be installed on all vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m, except for chassis-cabs.
The SM1 type of side-marker lamp shall be used on all categories of vehicles, however the SM2 type of side-marker lamp may be used on the M1 category of vehicles.

On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility requirements of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2. and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.
The minimum number of side-marker lamps per side shall be such that the rules for longitudinal positioning are complied with.
The side-marker lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 91, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The side-marker lamp shall be positioned in height above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).

At least one side-marker lamp shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle, except that for vehicles the length of which does not exceed 6 m and for chassis-cabs it is sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted within the first third and/or within the last third of the vehicle length, and for M1 vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m but does not exceed 7 m it is sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length.
The foremost side-marker lamp shall be not further than 3 m (4 m for semi-trailers) from the front of the vehicle.
The distance between two adjacent side-marker lamps shall not exceed 3 m, or 4 m if the structure, design or the operational use of the vehicle makes it impossible to comply with the 3 m requirement.
The distance between the rearmost side-marker lamp and the rear of the vehicle shall not exceed 1 m.

The side-marker lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° to the front and to the rear, which can be reduced to 30° for vehicles on which the installation of the side-marker lamps is optional.

Where the side-marker lamps are used to supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front and rear direction indicator lamps conforming to paragraph 6.5.5.2. and/or position lamps conforming to paragraphs 6.9.5.2. and 6.10.5.2., the horizontal angles of geometric visibility shall be 45° towards the front and rear ends of the vehicle and 30° towards the centre of the vehicle.

The side-marker lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 10° above and below the horizontal, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.

On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, amber side-marker lamps wired to flash shall flash in phase and at the same frequency with the direction-indicator lamps at the same side of the vehicle.
Where direction indicator lamps of category 5 are installed according to paragraph 6.5.3.1. on the side of the vehicle, amber side-marker lamps shall not flash.
If a tell-tale for the side-marker lamps exists, its function shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the front and rear position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the side-marker lamps shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
Rear side-marker lamps shall be amber if they flash with the rear direction-indicator lamp.

The distance in width between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces of the daytime running lamps in the direction of the reference axes shall not be less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
The daytime running lamp shall be positioned in height above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm.

The daytime running lamps shall be positioned in length at the front of the vehicle, this requirement being deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver either directly or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.

The daytime running lamps shall be switched ON automatically when the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position which makes it possible for the propulsion system to operate and neither the front fog lamps are switched ON, nor the headlamps are manually switched ON (except when they are used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals), nor the conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

The automatic operation of the daytime running lamps shall be resumed as soon as the conditions permitting them to remain OFF or be switched OFF manually (automatic transmission control in the park position, parking brake in the locked position, prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system, or vehicle speed not exceeding 15 km/h) no longer exist.

The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position which makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the front fog lamps are switched ON.
The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the headlamps are manually switched ON, except when they are used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals.
The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON, except that the rear position lamps and the other lamp(s) mentioned in paragraph 5.11. may be switched OFF and remain switched OFF as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).

If a front direction-indicator lamp is not reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp and the distance between the edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the front direction-indicator lamp and the daytime running lamp is equal or less than 40 mm, the electrical connections of the daytime running lamp shall be such that either the daytime running lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp, or its luminous intensity is reduced during that entire period to attain not more than 140 cd within the angles of geometric visibility, unless the luminous intensity of the front direction-indicator lamp in HV is at least 50% higher than the luminous intensity of the daytime running lamp in HV.

If a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp with totally common apparent surfaces, the electrical connections shall be such that the daytime running lamp function on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp.

If a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp with partially common apparent surfaces, the electrical connections of the daytime running lamp shall be such that either (a) the whole daytime running lamp function on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of activation of the front direction-indicator lamp, or (b) for category 1a or 1b front direction-indicator lamp the daytime running lamp function on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF for the part of the apparent surface in common with the one of the front direction indicator lamp and the luminous intensity of the part of the apparent surface not in common is reduced during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp, to attain not more than 140 cd within the angles of geometric visibility.
The emergency stop signal shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.
The emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop or direction-indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.

The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.

The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided or if the hazard warning signal is activated.
Where a rear-end collision alert signal is fitted, it shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the direction indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.25.7.
All the lamps of the rear-end collision alert signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 +/- 1.0 Hz.
The rear-end collision alert signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The rear-end collision alert signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.
The rear-end collision alert signal shall not be switched ON if the direction indicator lamps, the hazard warning signal or the emergency stop signal is activated.
The switch ON period of the rear-end collision alert signal shall be not more than 3 seconds.
The position in width of the lamp used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The position in height of the lamp used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The position in length of the lamp used for the answer-back signal shall be in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the answer-back signal.
The answer-back signal shall only operate under the park condition of a vehicle.
If the answer-back signal flashes, the frequency of the answer-back signal shall not exceed 2.0 Hz.

The answer-back signal shall be provided by approved lighting and light-signalling devices and exterior courtesy lamps where in all these cases the maximum luminous intensity per lamp does not exceed 700 cd on or above the HH line.
Front fog lamps, rear fog lamps and stop lamps shall not be used to provide the answer-back signal.

The duration of the optical indication of the answer-back signal, defined from the beginning to the end of the signal irrespective of whether it contains flashes, variations of intensity or variations in apparent surface, shall not exceed 3 seconds.

The visibility of a red lamp to the front and of a white lamp to the rear shall be assessed within zones 1 and 2 bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground, and in width by two vertical planes which, forming to the front and to the rear respectively an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width, where, if there are several points of contact, the foremost shall correspond to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.

The position of lamps, as defined in paragraph 2.1.6., in width, in height and in length, checked in accordance with paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4., shall be such that the measured distances fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The angles of geometric visibility of lamps, checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7., shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall comply with paragraph 5.10.
Every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle and its tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of UN R48.
Every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle and its tell-tales shall function in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps, as verified by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. of UN R48 are fulfilled.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps, as verified by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
